chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Replacing a bass drum head every time a drunk punched through it
summary: A patron broke his bass drum head each fortnight and paid $5; he soaked and tucked new calfskin heads by hand in a wash tub.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, there was a guy that used to come there every other Saturday -- he would come, and as soon as he would get drunk, the first thing he'd do was come up to the bandstand and knock a hole in my base drum. And I used to get so mad, but I had to smile because back in those days, you had better smile, so I smiled, but I didn't like it too well.

But then he would give me $5. Well, at that time, drums heads, you had to buy them loose -- they wasn't already tucked on to the drum, and so I was able to go to the music store down there on Flagley Street -- the music store was owned by Mr. Armandon and his wife, and he would sell me a base drum head for $3. So I used to make $2 on the deal every other week.
So, anyway, I would go over and take this drum head home and soak it in one of those number three tubs until it got soft, and I would take a spoon and ...
What's a number three tub, Panama?
That's a wash tub. That's what you used to bathe in all the time; they didn't have no bathtubs.
Well, how come they had numbers on them?

Sure. It was number one and number three was the big one. So I used to take the number three tub and soak my drum head in it, and then I would get a spoon and get out on the back porch and I would tuck it and then put it onto the bass drum.
What would you need a spoon for?
An eating spoon, a spoon that you eat with, you used the handle of the spoon to tuck the drum head on to the rim. That's how you used to do it.
Yeah, and tuck it on to the rim.
Like putting a tie on or something.

That's right, and this was the same principle. So you tuck it on and then you put it on to the bass drum which, at that time, was a 28-inch bass drum, so you had to tuck like the four corners first, you tucked like four on one side and then you tucked the other side, and then the other side, and then you would go and put the others in so

it'd be smooth, and then you put it on to the drum, and you'd put it on just enough so that the rim would hold it, because when it dried, it would tighten up and then you would put some more water on it so it would loosen up a bit and then you would turn the bolts around to tighten it up a little more.
And this was how you used to have to put the bass drum head on.
How long did it take to get the head set?
Oh, it would take about a day.
But it took you a whole night, like about 12 hours, for it to soak and get soft.
